questions.question: Which role is required to configure TPRM properties?

explanation.correct: The sn_vdr_risk_asmt.vendor_risk_admin role is required to configure TPRM properties. This administrative role has the permissions necessary to modify system settings and property values.

wrongAnswers.explanation: The vendor_assessor role is for users who assess third-party risk, not configure system properties
The vendor_risk_manager role manages risk assessments but doesn't configure system properties
The vendor_contact role is for third-party external users, not internal configuration

questions.question: Which applications must be activated to fully implement TPRM? (Choose THREE)

explanation.correct: To fully implement TPRM, you need to activate: Third-party Risk Management app, Due diligence request workflow application, and Vendor Risk Management Workspace application. These three applications together provide the complete TPRM functionality.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Customer Service Management is a separate application for customer service operations
Field Service Management is for managing field service operations, not third-party risk

references: TPRM Documentation - Configuring Third-party Risk Management

source.excerpt: Activate the Third-party Risk Management app [com.sn_vdr_risk_asmt], Activate the Due diligence request workflow application [com.sn_tprm_dd], Activate the Vendor Risk Management Workspace application [sn_vrm_ws].

questions.question: What is the purpose of the 'Organization name' property [sn_vdr_risk_asmt.company.name] in TPRM?

options.text: To set the default currency for assessments
Third-party contacts see this name in all references on the Third-party portal
To set the company logo on reports

explanation.correct: The Organization name property [sn_vdr_risk_asmt.company.name] defines the name that third-party contacts see in all references on the Third-party portal. This helps maintain consistent branding and identification.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Currency settings are not controlled by the Organization name property
Email notification configurations are separate from the Organization name property
Company logo settings are handled through different configuration options

source.excerpt: Organization name [sn_vdr_risk_asmt.company.name]: Third-party contacts see this name in all references on the Third-party portal.

questions.question:
Evaluate the following statements about TPRM configuration:

Statement 1: After the Smart Assessment Engine enabled property is set to true, this selection cannot be reversed.

Statement 2: Sample questionnaires are automatically included when installing TPRM regardless of installation options.

Which statements are TRUE?

explanation.correct: Statement 1 is true - after the Smart Assessment Engine enabled property is set to true, this selection cannot be reversed. Statement 2 is false - sample questionnaires are only included if you select 'Load demo data' while installing the app.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Statement 2 is false - demo data must be explicitly selected during installation
Statement 1 is true, Statement 2 is false
Statement 1 is correct - SAE enabling cannot be reversed

references: TPRM Documentation - Configuring Third-party Risk Management

source.excerpt: Warning: You won't be able to change this setting back once it's set to be 'true.' After this property is enabled, this selection can't be reversed.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a standard setup task when configuring TPRM?

options.text: Add an authentication policy for external third parties
Assign TPRM roles to users and user groups
Enable email communication with third-party contacts

explanation.correct: Configuring CMDB discovery schedules is not a TPRM setup task - it's related to Discovery and CMDB applications. Standard TPRM setup tasks include: authentication policies, role assignments, property configuration, email communication setup, and third-party contact configuration.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Adding authentication policies for third parties is a required TPRM setup task
Assigning TPRM roles is a required setup task for proper user management
Enabling email with third-party contacts is a setup task for communication

references: TPRM Documentation - Configuring Third-party Risk Management

source.excerpt: Setup tasks include: Activate applications, Add authentication policy, Assign TPRM roles, Add users to groups, Configure TPRM properties, Enable emails with third-party contacts.

questions.question: An administrator wants to allow TPR assessors to answer questions on behalf of third-party contacts. Which property should be configured?

explanation.correct: The sn_svdp.allow_assessor_edit property controls whether TPR assessors can answer or edit questionnaires for third-party contacts. Setting it to 'Enter answer' enables assessors to answer questions, 'Enter edit' enables them to modify responses, and 'false' disables both capabilities.

wrongAnswers.explanation: This property sets the organization name displayed in the portal
This property controls the maximum Excel file size for imports
This property controls the maximum age for questionnaire response reuse

source.excerpt: Allow assessors to answer/edit questionnaires for third-party contacts [sn_svdp.allow_assessor_edit]: Enter answer to enable TPR assessors to answer questions or modify responses.

questions.question: Which of the following can be imported from other systems into TPRM without being charged? (Choose THREE)

explanation.correct: TPRM allows importing existing data including third parties, engagements, assessments, questionnaires, and issues from other systems like Aravo or ProcessUnity without being charged. This facilitates migration from legacy systems.

wrongAnswers.explanation: License keys are not part of TPRM data imports
Authentication tokens are not imported as TPRM data

references: TPRM Documentation - Configuring Third-party Risk Management

source.excerpt: Import existing data (third parties, engagements, assessments, questionnaires, issues, and so on) from other systems (like the Aravo platform, the ProcessUnity platform, and so on). You aren't charged for importing the data.

questions.question: Where do administrators navigate to assign TPRM roles to user groups?

options.text: All > Third-party Risk Management > Administration > User Groups
All > System Security > Users and Groups > Groups
All > Third-party Risk Management > External Risk Assessments > All Assessments

explanation.correct: To assign TPRM roles, administrators navigate to All > Third-party Risk Management > Administration > User Groups. From there, they can select the Roles related list and assign appropriate TPRM roles (prefixed with sn_vdr) to groups.

wrongAnswers.explanation: While this is a valid system path for groups, the TPRM-specific path provides better context for TPRM role assignment
This is not the correct navigation path for TPRM role assignment
This path navigates to assessments, not user group configuration

references: TPRM Documentation - Assign TPRM roles to users and user groups

source.excerpt: Navigate to All > Third-party Risk Management > Administration > User Groups. Select the Roles related list to assign roles to the group.

questions.question: Which three applications must be activated during TPRM initial setup? (Choose THREE)

explanation.correct: The three applications that must be activated during TPRM setup are: Third-party Risk Management [com.sn_vdr_risk_asmt], Due diligence request workflow [com.sn_tprm_dd], and Vendor Risk Management Workspace [sn_vrm_ws].

wrongAnswers.explanation: GRC: Policy and Compliance Management is a separate optional integration, not required for TPRM setup
Enterprise Risk Management is a separate GRC application, not required for TPRM activation

source.excerpt: Activate the Third-party Risk Management app [com.sn_vdr_risk_asmt]. Activate the Due diligence request workflow application [com.sn_tprm_dd]. Activate the Vendor Risk Management Workspace application [sn_vrm_ws].

questions.question: What happens when you select 'Load demo data' while installing the TPRM application?

options.text: Sample third-party records and engagements are created
Sample questions for your question bank are included
Test user accounts are automatically generated
Sample risk intelligence provider integrations are configured

explanation.correct: The base system includes many sample questions that you can use in your question bank. To include sample questionnaires, select Load demo data while installing the app.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Loading demo data specifically includes sample questionnaires and questions, not pre-built third-party records
Test user accounts are not generated by loading demo data
Risk intelligence provider integrations must be configured separately

source.excerpt: The base system includes many sample questions that you can use in your question bank. To include sample questionnaires, select Load demo data while installing the app.

questions.question: What is the purpose of running quick-start tests in TPRM?

options.text: To validate the performance of the TPRM application under load
To verify TPRM still works after configuration changes such as upgrades or application development
To automatically generate initial assessment questionnaires
To create sample third-party records for training purposes

explanation.correct: Quick-start tests verify that TPRM still works after configuration changes such as applying an upgrade or developing an application. You can copy and customize the quick-start tests to pass when using instance-specific data.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Quick-start tests are for functional verification, not performance testing
Quick-start tests verify functionality, not generate questionnaires
Quick-start tests are for validation, not for creating sample records

source.excerpt: Verify that TPRM still works after you make configuration changes such as applying an upgrade or developing an application. Copy and customize the quick-start tests to pass when using your instance-specific data.

questions.question: Can existing data be imported into TPRM from other systems like Aravo or ProcessUnity?

options.text: Yes, but there is an additional charge per record imported
No, all data must be entered manually
Yes, and you are not charged for importing the data
Only third-party records can be imported; engagements must be created manually

explanation.correct: You can import existing data (third parties, engagements, assessments, questionnaires, issues, and so on) from other systems like the Aravo platform, the ProcessUnity platform, and others. You aren't charged for importing the data.

wrongAnswers.explanation: There is no additional charge for importing data from other systems
Data import from other systems is supported and optional
All types of data can be imported including third parties, engagements, assessments, questionnaires, and issues

source.excerpt: Import existing data (third parties, engagements, assessments, questionnaires, issues, and so on) from other systems. You aren't charged for importing the data.

questions.question: What is the significance of assigning TPRM roles to users before implementing the application?

options.text: It enables automatic generation of reports
It simplifies process management and ensures users are promptly notified of tasks in their areas of responsibility
It automatically creates third-party records for each user
It configures the TPRM dashboard layout for each user

explanation.correct: Assigning roles in a well-organized manner simplifies and improves process management and helps to ensure that users are promptly notified of tasks in their areas of responsibility.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Report generation is not directly tied to role assignment
Third-party records are not created by assigning roles to users
Dashboard layout configuration is separate from role assignment

source.excerpt: Assigning roles in a well-organized manner simplifies and improves process management and helps to ensure that users are promptly notified of tasks in their areas of responsibility.
